overall: The dividing line in Korean is morphological, not orthographic: single-morpheme loanwords that entered ordinary Korean (클릭, 스크롤, 포커스, 로드, 리사이즈, 트리거, 타겟) are written in hangul even by authors who keep every other identifier in English, while multi-morpheme compound transliterations (키다운, 키업, 마우스다운, 마우스업, 마우스아웃) appear nowhere in real Korean writing. Five of eight upstream candidates are mechanical transliterations with no observed usage. On the imperative question Korean is structurally safe — an imperative requires a verb ending, so bare Sino-Korean nouns cannot be misread as commands. The two real defects are homograph collisions rather than bad translations: 블러 means CSS image blur and 액션 means the action-movie sense — both actively misleading in a way a round-trip test would never catch.
